newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's labour unions declare work dispute.
newsitem.headline: Israel's labour unions declare work dispute.

text.p: Israel's Histadrut umbrella labour federation on Sunday declared a work dispute, the first legal step toward declaring a general strike, a spokeswoman for the organisation said.
She told Reuters the earliest a strike could be called would be September 2, but emphasised that negotiations with the government might prevent a general strike.
"The decision was taken in the wake of the decisions the government took," spokeswoman Ronit Levy told Reuters.

Histadrut labour federation secretary-general Amir Peretz was to meet Israeli Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman later on Sunday. The two last met on Thursday in an attempt to reach a compromise on a controversial package of economic reforms but failed to agree.

That meeting followed cabinet approval on Wednesday night of 10 structural reforms, part of an effort to revive Israel's flagging economic growth. The reforms include privatisation, capital market and foreign currency reforms, and sectoral deregulation.
Histadrut says the reforms are a prescription for increasing unemployment and attack workers' rights.
